verses.zh: 除酵节（又名逾越节）近了。
verses.en: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread,[NOTE:1] which is called the Passover, was approaching.
notes: The Feast of Unleavened Bread was a week long celebration that followed the day of Passover, so one name was used for both feasts (Exod 12:1-20; 23:15; 34:18; Deut 16:1-8).

verses.zh: 祭司长和文士想法子怎么才能杀害耶稣，是因他们惧怕百姓。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] chief priests and the experts in the law[NOTE:2] were trying to find some way[NOTE:3] to execute[NOTE:4] Jesus,[NOTE:5] for they were afraid of the people.[NOTE:6]
notes: Grk “And the.” Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Or “and the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 5:21.
Grk “were seeking how.”
The Greek verb here means “to get rid of by execution” (BDAG 64 s.v. ἀναιρέω 2; cf. also L&N 20.71, which states, “to get rid of someone by execution, often with legal or quasi-legal procedures”).
Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The suggestion here is that Jesus was too popular to openly arrest him. The verb were trying is imperfect. It suggests, in this context, that they were always considering the opportunities.

verses.zh: 这时，撒但入了那称为加略人犹大的心；他本是十二门徒里的一个。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Satan[NOTE:2] entered Judas, the one called Iscariot, who was one of the twelve.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
The cross is portrayed as part of the cosmic battle between Satan and God; see Luke 4:1-13; 11:14-23.
Grk “Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.”

verses.zh: 他去和祭司长并守殿官商量，怎么可以把耶稣交给他们。
verses.en: He went away and discussed with the chief priests and officers of the temple guard[NOTE:1] how he might[NOTE:2] betray Jesus,[NOTE:3] handing him over to them.[NOTE:4]
notes: The full title στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ (stratēgos tou hierou; “officer of the temple” or “captain of the temple guard”) is sometimes shortened to στρατηγός as here (L&N 37.91).
Luke uses this frequent indirect question to make his point (BDF §267.2).
Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “how he might hand him over to them,” in the sense of “betray him.”

verses.zh: 他们欢喜，就约定给他银子。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] were delighted[NOTE:2] and arranged to give him money.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

The leaders were delighted when Judas contacted them about betraying Jesus because it gave them the opportunity they had been looking for, and they could later claim that Jesus had been betrayed by one of his own disciples.
Matt 26:15 states the amount of money they gave Judas was thirty pieces of silver (see also Matt 27:3-4; Zech 11:12-13).

verses.zh: 他应允了，就找机会，要趁众人不在跟前的时候把耶稣交给他们。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] Judas[NOTE:2] agreed and began looking for an opportunity to betray Jesus[NOTE:3] when no crowd was present.[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the arrangement worked out in the preceding verse.
Grk “he”; the referent (Judas) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “betray him to them”; the referent of the first pronoun (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “apart from the crowd.”sn The leaders wanted to do this quietly, when no crowd was present, so no public uproar would result (cf. v. 21:38; 22:2).

verses.zh: 除酵节，须宰逾越羊羔的那一天到了。
verses.en: Then the day for the feast[NOTE:1] of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “for the feast” are not in the Greek text, but have been supplied for clarity.

Generally the feast of Unleavened Bread would refer to Nisan 15 (Friday), but the following reference to the sacrifice of the Passover lamb indicates that Nisan 14 (Thursday) was what Luke had in mind (Nisan = March 27 to April 25). The celebration of the Feast of Unleavened Bread lasted eight days, beginning with the Passover meal. The celebrations were so close together that at times the names of both were used interchangeably.

verses.zh: 耶稣打发彼得、约翰，说：「你们去为我们预备逾越节的筵席，好叫我们吃。」
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover[NOTE:2] for us to eat.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

This required getting a suitable lamb and finding lodging in Jerusalem where the meal could be eaten. The population of the city swelled during the feast, so lodging could be difficult to find. The Passover was celebrated each year in commemoration of the Israelites’ deliverance from Egypt; thus it was a feast celebrating redemption (see Exod 12). The Passover lamb was roasted and eaten after sunset in a family group of at least ten people (m. Pesahim 7.13). People ate the meal while reclining (see the note on table in 22:14). It included, besides the lamb, unleavened bread and bitter herbs as a reminder of Israel’s bitter affliction at the hands of the Egyptians. Four cups of wine mixed with water were also used for the meal. For a further description of the meal and the significance of the wine cups, see E. Ferguson, Backgrounds of Early Christianity, 523-24.
Grk “for us, so that we may eat.”

verses.zh: 他们问他说：「要我们在哪里预备？」
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare[NOTE:2] it?”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
In the Greek text this a deliberative subjunctive.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你们进了城，必有人拿着一瓶水迎面而来，你们就跟着他，到他所进的房子里去，
verses.en: He said to them, “Listen,[NOTE:1] when you have entered the city, a man carrying a jar of water[NOTE:2] will meet you.[NOTE:3] Follow him into the house that he enters,
notes: Grk “behold.”
Since women usually carried these jars, it would have been no problem for Peter and John to recognize the man Jesus was referring to.
Jesus is portrayed throughout Luke 22-23 as very aware of what will happen, almost directing events. Here this is indicated by his prediction that a man carrying a jar of water will meet you.

verses.zh: 对那家的主人说：『夫子说：客房在哪里？我与门徒好在那里吃逾越节的筵席。』
verses.en: and tell the owner of the house,[NOTE:1] ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
notes: Grk “to the master of the household,” referring to one who owns and manages the household, including family, servants, and slaves (L&N 57.14).

verses.zh: 他必指给你们摆设整齐的一间大楼，你们就在那里预备。」
verses.en: Then he will show you a large furnished room upstairs. Make preparations there.”

verses.zh: 他们去了，所遇见的正如耶稣所说的；他们就预备了逾越节的筵席。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they went and found things[NOTE:2] just as he had told them,[NOTE:3] and they prepared the Passover.
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of Jesus’ instructions.
The word “things” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.
The author’s note that the disciples found things just as he had told them shows that Jesus’ word could be trusted.

verses.zh: 时候到了，耶稣坐席，使徒也和他同坐。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] when the hour came, Jesus[NOTE:2] took his place at the table[NOTE:3] and the apostles joined[NOTE:4] him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Grk “reclined at table,” as 1st century middle eastern meals were not eaten while sitting at a table, but while reclining on one’s side on the floor with the head closest to the low table and the feet farthest away.
Grk “the apostles with him.”

verses.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「我很愿意在受害以先和你们吃这逾越节的筵席。
verses.en: And he said to them, “I have earnestly desired[NOTE:1] to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
notes: This phrase parallels a Hebrew infinitive absolute and serves to underline Jesus’ enthusiasm for holding this meal (BDF §198.6).

verses.zh: 我告诉你们，我不再吃这筵席，直到成就在　神的国里。」
verses.en: For I tell you, I will not eat it again[NOTE:1] until it is fulfilled[NOTE:2] in the kingdom of God.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Although the word “again” is not in the Greek text, it is supplied to indicate that Jesus did indeed partake of this Passover meal, as statements in v. 18 suggest (“from now on”). For more complete discussion see D. L. Bock, Luke (BECNT), 2:1720.

Jesus looked to a celebration in the kingdom to come when the Passover is fulfilled. This reference could well suggest that some type of commemorative sacrifice and meal will be celebrated then, as the antecedent is the Passover sacrifice. The reference is not to the Lord’s supper as some argue, but the Passover.
The kingdom of God here refers to the kingdom in all its power. See Luke 17:20-37.

verses.zh: 耶稣接过杯来，祝谢了，说：「你们拿这个，大家分着喝。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he took a cup,[NOTE:2] and after giving thanks he said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

Then he took a cup. Only Luke mentions two cups at this meal; the other synoptic gospels (Matt, Mark) mention only one. This is the first of the two. It probably refers to the first cup in the traditional Passover meal, which today has four cups (although it is debated whether the fourth cup was used in the 1st century).

verses.zh: 我告诉你们，从今以后，我不再喝这葡萄汁，直等　神的国来到。」
verses.en: For I tell you that from now on I will not drink of the fruit[NOTE:1] of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “the produce” (“the produce of the vine” is a figurative expression for wine).
Until the kingdom of God comes is a reference to the kingdom in all its power. See Luke 17:20-37. Jesus awaits celebration with the arrival of full kingdom blessing.

verses.zh: 又拿起饼来，祝谢了，就擘开，递给他们，说：「这是我的身体，为你们舍的，你们也应当如此行，为的是记念我。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he took bread, and after giving thanks he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body[NOTE:2] which is given for you.[NOTE:3] Do this in remembrance of me.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

Some significant Western witnesses (D it) lack the words from this point to the end of v. 20. However, the authenticity of these verses is very likely. It is found in a variety of witnesses that represent a broad geographical base (P75 א A B C L Tvid W Δ Θ Ψ ƒ1,13 M al co), rendering the rise of the shorter reading much easier of explanation than the reverse. Further, the inclusion of the second cup is the harder reading, since it differs from Matt 26:26-29 and Mark 14:22-25. Further discussion of this complicated problem (the most difficult in Luke) can be found in TCGNT 148-50.
The language of the phrase given for you alludes to Christ’s death in our place. It is a powerful substitutionary image of what he did for us.

verses.zh: 饭后也照样拿起杯来，说：「这杯是用我血所立的新约，是为你们流出来的。
verses.en: And in the same way he took[NOTE:1] the cup after they had eaten,[NOTE:2] saying, “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant[NOTE:3] in my blood.
notes: The words “he took” are not in the Greek text at this point, but are an understood repetition from v. 19.
The phrase “after they had eaten” translates the temporal infinitive construction μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι (meta to deipnēsai), where the verb δειπνέω (deipneō) means “to eat a meal” or “to have a meal.”
Jesus’ death established the forgiveness promised in the new covenant of Jer 31:31. Jesus is reinterpreting the symbolism of the Passover meal, indicating the presence of a new era.

verses.zh: 看哪，那卖我之人的手与我一同在桌子上。
verses.en: “But look, the hand of the one who betrays[NOTE:1] me is with me on the table.[NOTE:2]
notes: The one who betrays me. Jesus knows about Judas and what he has done.

The point of Jesus’ comment here is not to identify the specific individual per se, but to indicate that it is one who was close to him—somebody whom no one would suspect. His comment serves to heighten the treachery of Judas’ betrayal.

verses.zh: 人子固然要照所预定的去世，但卖人子的人有祸了！」
verses.en: For the Son of Man is to go just as it has been determined,[NOTE:1] but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!”
notes: Jesus’ death has been determined as a part of God’s plan (Acts 2:22-24).

verses.zh: 他们就彼此对问，是哪一个要做这事。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they began to question one another as to which of them it could possibly be who would do this.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of Jesus’ comments: The disciples begin wondering who would betray him.

verses.zh: 门徒起了争论，他们中间哪一个可算为大。
verses.en: A dispute also started[NOTE:1] among them over which of them was to be regarded as the greatest.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “happened.”
Though the term μείζων (meizōn) here is comparative in form, it is superlative in sense (BDF §244).

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「外邦人有君王为主治理他们，那掌权管他们的称为恩主。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] said to them, “The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the dispute among the apostles.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The title ‘benefactor,’ highlighting grace and meaning something like “helper of the people,” was even given to tyrants (2 Macc 4:2; 3 Macc 3:19; Josephus, J. W. 3.9.8 [3.459]).

verses.zh: 但你们不可这样；你们里头为大的，倒要像年幼的，为首领的，倒要像服事人的。
verses.en: Not so with you;[NOTE:1] instead the one who is greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the leader[NOTE:2] like the one who serves.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “But you are not thus.”
Or “the ruler.”

And the leader like the one who serves. Leadership was not to be a matter of privilege and special status, but of service. All social status is leveled out by these remarks. Jesus himself is the prime example of the servant-leader.

verses.zh: 是谁为大？是坐席的呢？是服事人的呢？不是坐席的大吗？然而，我在你们中间如同服事人的。
verses.en: For who is greater, the one who is seated at the table,[NOTE:1] or the one who serves? Is it not[NOTE:2] the one who is seated at the table? But I am among you as one[NOTE:3] who serves.
notes: Grk “who reclines at table,” as 1st century middle eastern meals were not eaten while sitting at a table, but while reclining on one’s side on the floor with the head closest to the low table and the feet farthest away.
The interrogative particle used here in the Greek text (οὐχί, ouchi) expects a positive reply.
Jesus’ example of humble service, as one who serves, shows that the standard for a disciple is different from that of the world. For an example see John 13:1-17.

verses.zh: 我在磨炼之中，常和我同在的就是你们。
verses.en: “You are the ones who have remained[NOTE:1] with me in my trials.
notes: Or “continued” (L&N 34.3). Jesus acknowledges the disciples’ faithfulness.

verses.zh: 我将国赐给你们，正如我父赐给我一样，
verses.en: Thus[NOTE:1] I grant[NOTE:2] to you a kingdom,[NOTE:3] just as my Father granted to me,
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “thus” to indicate the implied result of the disciples’ perseverance with Jesus.

With the statement “I grant to you a kingdom” Jesus gave the disciples authority over the kingdom, as God had given him such authority. The present tense looks at authority given presently, though the major manifestation of its presence is yet to come as the next verse shows.
Or “I give you the right to rule” (cf. CEV). For this translation of διατίθεμαι βασιλείαν (diatithemai basileian) see L&N 37.105.

verses.zh: 叫你们在我国里，坐在我的席上吃喝，并且坐在宝座上，审判以色列十二个支派。」
verses.en: that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and you will sit[NOTE:1] on thrones judging[NOTE:2] the 12 tribes of Israel.
notes: This verb is future indicative, and thus not subordinate to “grant” (διατίθεμαι, diatithemai) as part of the result clause beginning with ἵνα ἔσθητε (hina esthēte) at the beginning of v. 30. It is better understood as a predictive future.
The statement you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel looks at the future authority the Twelve will have when Jesus returns. They will share in Israel’s judgment.

verses.zh: 主又说：「西门！西门！撒但想要得着你们，好筛你们像筛麦子一样；
verses.en: “Simon,[NOTE:1] Simon, pay attention![NOTE:2] Satan has demanded to have you all,[NOTE:3] to sift you like wheat,[NOTE:4]
notes: The majority of mss (א A D W Θ Ψ ƒ1,13 M as well as several versional witnesses) begin this verse with an introductory comment, “and the Lord said,” indicating a change in the subject of discussion. But this is apparently a reading motivated by the need for clarity. Some of the best witnesses, along with a few others (P75 B L T 1241 2542c sys co), do not contain these words. The abrupt shift is the more difficult reading and thus more likely to be autographic.
Grk “behold” (for “pay attention” see L&N 91.13).
This pronoun is plural in the Greek text, so it refers to all the disciples of which Peter is the representative.
Satan has demanded permission to put them to the test. The idiom “sift (someone) like wheat” is similar to the English idiom “to pick (someone) apart.” The pronoun you is implied.

verses.zh: 但我已经为你祈求，叫你不至于失了信心。你回头以后，要坚固你的弟兄。」
verses.en: but I have prayed for you, Simon,[NOTE:1] that your faith may not fail.[NOTE:2] When[NOTE:3] you have turned back,[NOTE:4] strengthen[NOTE:5] your brothers.”
notes: Here and in the remainder of the verse the second person pronouns are singular, so only Peter is in view. The name “Simon” has been supplied as a form of direct address to make this clear in English.
That your faith may not fail. Note that Peter’s denials are pictured here as lapses, not as a total absence of faith.
Grk “And when.” Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Or “turned around.”
Strengthen your brothers refers to Peter helping to strengthen their faith. Jesus quite graciously restores Peter “in advance,” even with the knowledge of his approaching denials.

verses.zh: 彼得说：「主啊，我就是同你下监，同你受死，也是甘心！」
verses.en: But Peter[NOTE:1] said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Peter) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The confidence Peter has in private (Lord, I am ready…) will wilt under the pressure of the public eye.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「彼得，我告诉你，今日鸡还没有叫，你要三次说不认得我。」
verses.en: Jesus replied,[NOTE:1] “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow[NOTE:2] today until you have denied[NOTE:3] three times that you know me.”
notes: Grk “he said”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
That is, Peter’s denials will happen before the sun rises.
Once again, Jesus is quite aware that Peter will deny him. Peter, however, is too nonchalant about the possibility of stumbling.

verses.zh: 耶稣又对他们说：「我差你们出去的时候，没有钱囊，没有口袋，没有鞋，你们缺少甚么没有？」他们说：「没有。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] said to them, “When I sent you out with no money bag,[NOTE:3] or traveler’s bag,[NOTE:4] or sandals, you didn’t lack[NOTE:5] anything, did you?” They replied,[NOTE:6] “Nothing.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Traditionally, “purse” (likewise in v. 36).
Or possibly “beggar’s bag” (L&N 6.145).
This refers back to 9:3 and 10:3-4. The Greek construction anticipates a negative reply which is indicated in the translation by the ‘tag’ at the end, “did you?” Nothing was lacking.
Grk “said.”

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「但如今有钱囊的可以带着，有口袋的也可以带着，没有刀的要卖衣服买刀。
verses.en: He said to them, “But now, the one who[NOTE:1] has a money bag must take it, and likewise a traveler’s bag[NOTE:2] too. And the one who has no sword must sell his cloak and buy one.
notes: The syntax of this verse is disputed, resulting in various translations. The major options are either (1) that reflected in the translation or (2) that those who have a money bag and traveler’s bag should get a sword, just as those who do not have these items should sell their cloak to buy a sword. The point of all the options is that things have changed and one now needs full provisions. Opposition will come. But “sword” is a figure for preparing to fight. See Luke 22:50-51.
Or possibly “beggar’s bag” (L&N 6.145).

verses.zh: 我告诉你们，经上写着说：『他被列在罪犯之中。』这话必应验在我身上；因为那关系我的事必然成就。」
verses.en: For I tell you that this scripture must be[NOTE:1] fulfilled in me, ‘And he was counted with the transgressors.’[NOTE:2] For what is written about me is being fulfilled.”[NOTE:3]
notes: This scripture must be fulfilled in me. The statement again reflects the divine necessity of God’s plan. See 4:43-44.
This is a quotation from Isa 53:12. It highlights a theme of Luke 22-23. Though completely innocent, Jesus dies as if he were a criminal.tn Or “with the lawless.”
Grk “is having its fulfillment.”

verses.zh: 他们说：「主啊，请看！这里有两把刀。」耶稣说：「够了。」
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they said, “Look, Lord, here are two swords.”[NOTE:2] Then he told them, “It is enough.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of Jesus’ comments about obtaining swords.
Here are two swords. The disciples mistakenly took Jesus to mean that they should prepare for armed resistance, something he will have to correct in 22:50-51.
It is enough. The disciples’ misunderstanding caused Jesus to terminate the discussion.

verses.zh: 耶稣出来，照常往橄榄山去，门徒也跟随他。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] went out and made his way,[NOTE:3] as he customarily did, to the Mount of Olives,[NOTE:4] and the disciples followed him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “went.”
See the note on the Mount of Olives in Luke 19:29.

verses.zh: 到了那地方，就对他们说：「你们要祷告，免得入了迷惑。」
verses.en: When he came to the place,[NOTE:1] he said to them, “Pray that you will not fall into temptation.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Luke does not mention Gethsemane by name, but calls it simply the place.

Jesus’ instructions to pray not to fall into temptation is an allusion to Luke 22:28-38, especially 22:31. The temptation is Satan’s challenge to them to defect, like what happened to Judas and what will happen to Peter.

verses.zh: 于是离开他们约有扔一块石头那么远，跪下祷告，
verses.en: He went away from them about a stone’s throw, knelt down, and prayed,

verses.zh: 说：「父啊！你若愿意，就把这杯撤去；然而，不要成就我的意思，只要成就你的意思。」
verses.en: “Father, if you are willing, take[NOTE:1] this cup[NOTE:2] away from me. Yet not my will but yours[NOTE:3] be done.” [
notes: Luke’s term παρένεγκε is not as exact as the one in Matt 26:39. Luke’s means “take away” (BDAG 772 s.v. παρένεγκε 2.c) while Matthew’s means “take away without touching,” suggesting an alteration (if possible) in God’s plan. For further discussion see D. L. Bock, Luke (BECNT), 2:1759-60.
This cup alludes to the wrath of God that Jesus would experience (in the form of suffering and death) for us. See Pss 11:6; 75:8-9; Isa 51:17, 19, 22 for this figure.
With the statement “Not my will but yours be done” Jesus submitted fully to God’s will.

verses.zh: 有一位天使从天上显现，加添他的力量。
verses.en: Then an angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him.

verses.zh: 耶稣极其伤痛，祷告更加恳切，汗珠如大血点滴在地上。
verses.en: And in his anguish[NOTE:1] he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat was like drops of blood falling to the ground.][NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “And being in anguish.”

Angelic aid is noted elsewhere in the gospels: Matt 4:11 = Mark 1:13.tc Several significant Greek mss (P75 א1 A B N T W 579 1071*) along with diverse and widespread versional witnesses lack 22:43-44. In addition, the verses are placed after Matt 26:39 by ƒ13. Floating texts typically suggest both spuriousness and early scribal impulses to regard the verses as historically authentic. These verses are included in א*,2 D L Θ Ψ 0171 ƒ1 M lat Ju Ir Hipp Eus. However, a number of mss mark the text with an asterisk or obelisk, indicating the scribe’s assessment of the verses as inauthentic. At the same time, these verses generally fit Luke’s style. Arguments can be given on both sides about whether scribes would tend to include or omit such comments about Jesus’ humanity and an angel’s help. But even if the verses are not literarily authentic, they are probably historically authentic. This is due to the fact that this text was well known in several different locales from a very early period. Since there are no synoptic parallels to this account and since there is no obvious reason for adding these words here, it is very likely that such verses recount a part of the actual suffering of our Lord. Nevertheless, because of the serious doubts as to these verses’ authenticity, they have been put in brackets. For an important discussion of this problem, see B. D. Ehrman and M. A. Plunkett, “The Angel and the Agony: The Textual Problem of Luke 22:43-44, ” CBQ 45 (1983): 401-16.

verses.zh: 祷告完了，就起来，到门徒那里，见他们因为忧愁都睡着了，
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] he got up from prayer, he came to the disciples and found them sleeping, exhausted[NOTE:2] from grief.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

Grk “from grief.” The word “exhausted” is not in the Greek text, but is implied; the disciples have fallen asleep from mental and emotional exhaustion resulting from their distress (see L&N 25.273; cf. TEV, NIV, NLT).

verses.zh: 就对他们说：「你们为甚么睡觉呢？起来祷告，免得入了迷惑！」
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray that you will not fall into temptation!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of Jesus finding them asleep.
Jesus calls the disciples again to prayerful watchfulness with the words “Get up and pray” (see 22:40). The time is full of danger (22:53).

verses.zh: 说话之间，来了许多人。那十二个门徒里名叫犹大的，走在前头，就近耶稣，要与他亲嘴。
verses.en: While he was still speaking, suddenly a crowd appeared,[NOTE:1] and the man named Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He walked up[NOTE:2] to Jesus to kiss him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “While he was still speaking, behold, a crowd, and the one called Judas…was leading them.” The abrupt appearance of the crowd on the scene is indicated in the translation by “suddenly” and “appeared.”
Grk “drew near.”

Many mss (D Θ ƒ13 700 pm as well as several versional mss) add here, “for this is the sign he gave to them: Whoever I kiss is [the one].” This addition is almost certainly not original, since most of the significant mss lack it. It may be a copyist’s attempt to clarify the text, or the accidental inclusion of a marginal gloss.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他说：「犹大！你用亲嘴的暗号卖人子吗？」
verses.en: But Jesus said to him, “Judas, would you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Jesus’ comment about betraying the Son of Man with a kiss shows the hypocrisy and blindness of an attempt to cover up sin. On “misused kisses” in the Bible, see Gen 27:26-27; 2 Sam 15:5; Prov 7:13; 27:6; 2 Sam 20:9.

verses.zh: 左右的人见光景不好，就说：「主啊！我们拿刀砍可以不可以？」
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] those who were around him saw what was about to happen, they said, “Lord, should[NOTE:2] we use our swords?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
The direct question using “if” in Greek is not unusual (BDF §440.3).
“Should we use our swords?” The disciples’ effort to defend Jesus recalls Luke 22:35-38. One individual did not wait for the answer.

verses.zh: 内中有一个人把大祭司的仆人砍了一刀，削掉了他的右耳。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] one of them[NOTE:2] struck the high priest’s slave,[NOTE:3] cutting off his right ear.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
One of them. The unnamed disciple is Peter according to John 18:10 (cf. also Matt 26:51; Mark 14:47).
See the note on the word “slave” in 7:2.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「到了这个地步，由他们吧！」就摸那人的耳朵，把他治好了。
verses.en: But Jesus said,[NOTE:1] “Enough of this!” And he touched the man’s[NOTE:2] ear and healed[NOTE:3] him.
notes: Grk “But answering, Jesus said.” This is redundant in contemporary English and has been simplified in the translation.
Grk “his”; the referent (the slave of the high priest mentioned in the previous verse) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
When Jesus healed the man’s ear he showed grace even to those who hated him, following his own teaching (Luke 6:27-36).

verses.zh: 耶稣对那些来拿他的祭司长和守殿官并长老说：「你们带着刀棒出来拿我，如同拿强盗吗？
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus said to the chief priests, the officers of the temple guard,[NOTE:2] and the elders who had come out to get him, “Have you come out with swords and clubs like you would against an outlaw?[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

This title, literally “official of the temple” (στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ, stratēgos tou hierou), referred to the commander of the Jewish soldiers who guarded and maintained order in the Jerusalem temple. Here, since the term is plural, it has been translated “officers of the temple guard” rather than “commanders of the temple guard,” since the idea of a number of commanders might be confusing to the modern English reader.

Or “a revolutionary.” This term can refer to one who stirs up rebellion: BDAG 594 s.v. λῃστής 2 has “revolutionary, insurrectionist, guerrilla” citing evidence from Josephus (J. W. 2.13.2-3 [2.253-254]). However, this usage generally postdates Jesus’ time. It does refer to a figure of violence. Luke uses the same term for the highwaymen who attack the traveler in the parable of the good Samaritan (10:30).

verses.zh: 我天天同你们在殿里，你们不下手拿我。现在却是你们的时候，黑暗掌权了。」
verses.en: Day after day when I was with you in the temple courts,[NOTE:1] you did not arrest me.[NOTE:2] But this is your hour,[NOTE:3] and that of the power[NOTE:4] of darkness!”
notes: Grk “in the temple.”
Grk “lay hands on me.”
Or “your time.”
Or “authority,” “domain.”

verses.zh: 他们拿住耶稣，把他带到大祭司的宅里。彼得远远地跟着。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] they arrested[NOTE:2] Jesus,[NOTE:3] led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house.[NOTE:4] But Peter was following at a distance.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Or “seized” (L&N 37.109).
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Putting all the gospel accounts together, there is a brief encounter with Annas (brought him into the high priest’s house, here and John 18:13, where Annas is named); the meeting led by Caiaphas (Matt 26:57-68 = Mark 14:53-65); and then a Sanhedrin meeting (Matt 27:1; Mark 15:1; Luke 22:66-71). These latter two meetings might be connected and apparently went into the morning.

verses.zh: 他们在院子里生了火，一同坐着；彼得也坐在他们中间。
verses.en: When they had made a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.

verses.zh: 有一个使女看见彼得坐在火光里，就定睛看他，说：「这个人素来也是同那人一伙的。」
verses.en: Then a slave girl,[NOTE:1] seeing him as he sat in the firelight, stared at him and said, “This man was with him too!”
notes: The Greek term here is παιδίσκη (paidiskē), referring to a slave girl or slave woman.

verses.zh: 彼得却不承认，说：「女子，我不认得他。」
verses.en: But Peter[NOTE:1] denied it: “Woman,[NOTE:2] I don’t know[NOTE:3] him!”
notes: Grk “he denied it, saying.” The referent (Peter) has been specified in the translation for clarity. The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant and has not been translated.
Woman was a polite form of address (see BDAG 208-9 s.v. γυνή), similar to “Madam” or “Ma’am” used in English in different regions.
The expression “I do not know him” had an idiomatic use in Jewish ban formulas in the synagogue and could mean, “I have nothing to do with him.”

verses.zh: 过了不多的时候，又有一个人看见他，说：「你也是他们一党的。」彼得说：「你这个人！我不是。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] a little later someone else[NOTE:2] saw him and said, “You are one of them too.” But Peter said, “Man,[NOTE:3] I am not!”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
In Mark 14:69, the same slave girl made the charge. So apparently Peter was being identified by a variety of people.
Here and in v. 60 “Man” is used as a neutral form of address to a stranger.

verses.zh: 约过了一小时，又有一个人极力地说：「他实在是同那人一伙的，因为他也是加利利人。」
verses.en: And after about an hour still another insisted,[NOTE:1] “Certainly this man was with him because he too is a Galilean.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “insisted, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant in English and has not been translated here.
According to Mark 14:70 it was Peter’s accent that gave him away as a Galilean.

verses.zh: 彼得说：「你这个人！我不晓得你说的是甚么！」正说话之间，鸡就叫了。
verses.en: But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you’re talking about!” At that moment,[NOTE:1] while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “And immediately.” Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

A real rooster crowing is probably in view here (rather than the Roman trumpet call known as gallicinium), in part due to the fact that Mark 14:72 mentions the rooster crowing twice. See the discussion at Matt 26:74.

verses.zh: 主转过身来看彼得，彼得便想起主对他所说的话：「今日鸡叫以先，你要三次不认我。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the Lord turned and looked straight at Peter, and Peter remembered the word of the Lord,[NOTE:2] how he had said to him, “Before a rooster crows today, you will deny me three times.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

“The word of the Lord” is a technical expression in OT literature, often referring to a divine prophetic utterance (e.g., Gen 15:1, Isa 1:10, Jonah 1:1). In the NT it occurs 15 times: 3 times as ῥῆμα τοῦ κυρίου (rhēma tou kuriou; here and in Acts 11:16, 1 Pet 1:25) and 12 times as λόγος τοῦ κυρίου (logos tou kuriou; Acts 8:25; 13:44, 48, 49; 15:35, 36; 16:32; 19:10, 20; 1 Thess 1:8; 4:15; 2 Thess 3:1). As in the OT, this phrase focuses on the prophetic nature and divine origin of what has been said. Because of its technical nature the expression has been retained in the translation in preference to a smoother rendering like “remembered what the Lord had said” (cf. TEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 他就出去痛哭。
verses.en: And he went outside and wept bitterly.[NOTE:1]
notes: When Peter went out and wept bitterly it shows he really did not want to fail here and was deeply grieved that he had.

verses.zh: 看守耶稣的人戏弄他，打他，
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] the men who were holding Jesus[NOTE:2] under guard began to mock him and beat him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.
Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 又蒙着他的眼，问他说：「你是先知，告诉我们打你的是谁？」
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] blindfolded him and asked him repeatedly,[NOTE:2] “Prophesy! Who hit you?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
The verb ἐπηρώτων (epērōtōn) has been translated as an iterative imperfect. The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant in English and has not been translated here.
Grk “Who is the one who hit you?”sn Who hit you? This is a variation of one of three ancient games that involved blindfolds.

verses.zh: 他们还用许多别的话辱骂他。
verses.en: They also said many other things against him, reviling[NOTE:1] him.
notes: Or “insulting.” Luke uses a strong word here; it means “to revile, to defame, to blaspheme” (L&N 33.400).

verses.zh: 天一亮，民间的众长老连祭司长带文士都聚会，把耶稣带到他们的公会里，
verses.en: When day came, the council of the elders of the people gathered together, both the chief priests and the experts in the law.[NOTE:1] Then[NOTE:2] they led Jesus[NOTE:3] away to their council[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “and the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 5:21.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Their council is probably a reference to the Jewish Sanhedrin, the council of seventy leaders.

verses.zh: 说：「你若是基督，就告诉我们。」耶稣说：「我若告诉你们，你们也不信；
verses.en: and said, “If[NOTE:1] you are the Christ,[NOTE:2] tell us.” But he said to them, “If[NOTE:3] I tell you, you will not[NOTE:4] believe,
notes: This is a first class condition in the Greek text.
Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 2:11.
This is a third class condition in the Greek text. Jesus had this experience already in 20:1-8.
The negation in the Greek text is the strongest possible (οὐ μή, ou mē).

verses.zh: 我若问你们，你们也不回答。
verses.en: and if[NOTE:1] I ask you, you will not[NOTE:2] answer.
notes: This is also a third class condition in the Greek text.
The negation in the Greek text is the strongest possible (οὐ μή, ou mē).

verses.zh: 从今以后，人子要坐在　神权能的右边。」
verses.en: But from now on[NOTE:1] the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand[NOTE:2] of the power[NOTE:3] of God.”
notes: From now on. Jesus’ authority was taken up from this moment on. Ironically he is now the ultimate judge, who is himself being judged.

Seated at the right hand is an allusion to Ps 110:1 (“Sit at my right hand…”) and is a claim that Jesus shares authority with God in heaven. Those present may have thought they were his judges, but, in fact, the reverse was true.
The expression the right hand of the power of God is a circumlocution for referring to God. Such indirect references to God were common in 1st century Judaism out of reverence for the divine name.

verses.zh: 他们都说：「这样，你是　神的儿子吗？」耶稣说：「你们所说的是。」
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they all said, “Are you the Son of God,[NOTE:2] then?” He answered[NOTE:3] them, “You say[NOTE:4] that I am.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of Jesus’ pronouncement.
The members of the council understood the force of the claim and asked Jesus about another title, Son of God.
Grk “He said to them.”
Jesus’ reply, “You say that I am,” was not a denial, but a way of giving a qualified positive response: “You have said it, but I do not quite mean what you think.”

verses.zh: 他们说：「何必再用见证呢？他亲口所说的，我们都亲自听见了。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] they said, “Why do we need further testimony? We have heard it ourselves[NOTE:2] from his own lips!”[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

We have heard it ourselves. The Sanhedrin regarded the answer as convicting Jesus. They saw it as blasphemous to claim such intimacy and shared authority with God, a claim so serious and convicting that no further testimony was needed.
Grk “from his own mouth” (an idiom).
